skill.name: zach-feature-demand-validator
skill.description: Validates whether an Amazon product feature is real customer demand by comparing review evidence, keyword signals, and community discussion.
skill.summary: Evidence-based feature demand validation for Amazon product research.
skill.author: zach22-1999

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, fenced command examples, public source URLs, parser regexes, and readable documentation. The skill is not malicious, but it understates its risk because it requests file editing, Bash, and network tools while documenting automated repair and script workflows.

remediation.issue: The skill front matter marks the workflow as low risk despite broad file, shell, and network tools.
remediation.suggestion: Raise the declared risk level and clearly state that Bash, file writes, and web requests require user awareness.

remediation.issue: The troubleshooting prompt encourages automatic workspace repair.
remediation.suggestion: Revise the prompt to require a proposed change list and user confirmation before edits or command execution.

remediation.issue: Command examples accept user-selected input and output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to keep outputs inside a project-owned directory and avoid parsing untrusted review packs without inspection.

medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The broad allowed-tools list and low risk declaration are adjacent in the front matter. The workflow also includes local script execution and public web fetching.

low_findings.title: Overbroad Automatic Repair Prompt
low_findings.description: The README suggests asking an AI to inspect the current workspace and automatically repair issues if possible. This can cause unintended file changes without a clear confirmation boundary.
low_findings.confidence_reasoning: The troubleshooting prompt explicitly asks the AI to check related files and repair problems where possible. It appears operational rather than malicious, so the severity is low.

content.value_statement: Product teams often chase features without proof that customers care. This skill compares reviews, keyword signals, and community discussion to validate feature demand.
actual_capabilities: Guides review, keyword, and community evidence collection for Amazon feature validation.
Parses Sorftime product review exports into standardized review CSV files.
Parses local review_source_pack files from CSV, text, Markdown, or HTML.
Generates keyword and community CSV deliverables from structured source data.
Validates expected report, CSV, and review evidence package deliverables.
limitations: Results depend on current review, search, and community data quality.
Sorftime data is preferred; fallback web sources have lower precision.
The scripts classify sentiment with simple rating and keyword rules.
The skill does not make final product investment decisions.

use_cases.title: Validate a Micro-Feature
use_cases.description: Check whether customers mention, request, or reject a proposed feature before sourcing or tooling work.

use_cases.title: Compare Competitor Gaps
use_cases.description: Use reviews and search signals to decide whether a competitor feature is worth following.

use_cases.title: Prepare Evidence for Review
use_cases.description: Create a Markdown report and CSV evidence files for an internal product decision meeting.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with category and feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate whether steam is real customer demand for air fryers in the US market. Use reviews, keyword signals, and community discussion.

prompt_templates.title: Use an ASIN Baseline
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused analysis around a known product.
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate whether the self-cleaning feature on this ASIN is worth copying. Compare review sentiment, keyword demand, and competitor evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Run Fallback Review Pack
prompt_templates.scenario: No Sorftime access, but local review files are available.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my review_source_pack to validate foldable handle demand. Mark fallback limitations and keep all source fields in the CSV outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Evidence and Decide
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the feature validation report and CSV files. Identify weak evidence, negative signals, missing sources, and the safest product recommendation.

output_examples.input: Validate steam demand for air fryers in the US market.
output: A demand verdict with confidence level and action recommendation.
A review signal summary with feature mention rate and sentiment split.
Keyword and community signal summaries with source notes.

output_examples.input: Analyze a local review_source_pack for anti-drip demand.
output: A fallback report that states which dimensions were fully verified.
A standardized review CSV with source, raw file, and capture fields.
Warnings about missing keyword or community evidence.

output_examples.input: Check final deliverables for a feature validation project.
output_examples.output: A validation result that lists missing report files, missing CSV files, invalid ASIN values, or incomplete fallback evidence.

best_practices: Use real ASINs and record product names, sources, and capture dates.
Collect enough positive and negative reviews before drawing conclusions.
Separate data facts, public information, and analysis in the final report.
anti_patterns: Using placeholder ASINs or brand names as evidence.
Treating fallback keyword estimates as precise Sorftime data.
Ignoring negative feature feedback because it conflicts with the desired conclusion.

faq.question: What does this skill validate?
faq.answer: It validates whether a specific Amazon product feature appears to be real customer demand.

faq.question: Which evidence sources does it use?
faq.answer: It uses review data, keyword demand signals, and public community discussion.

faq.question: Does it require Sorftime?
faq.answer: Sorftime is preferred, but the skill includes fallback workflows for local review packs and public web sources.

faq.question: Can it make the product decision for me?
faq.answer: No. It provides an evidence-based recommendation for a human product decision.

faq.question: What files can it produce?
faq.answer: It can guide creation of a Markdown validation report and five standardized CSV evidence files.

faq.question: What should users verify before trusting results?
faq.answer: Users should verify ASINs, source URLs, data recency, sample size, and any fallback limitations.
